newsitem.title: ZIMBABWE: Zimbabwe shares weaken on profit-taking.
newsitem.headline: Zimbabwe shares weaken on profit-taking.

text.p: Zimbabwean shares traded largely weaker on continuing profit-taking with brokers saying new fuel price hikes had probably made investors cautious about prospects of lower annual inflation and interest rates.

The 57-share industrial index dropped 70.55 points to close at 6,831.24, depressed largely by Alloys' 95-cent slide to 830 and publishing group Zimpapers and cement producer Porthold's 50-cent each losses to 1,400 and 1,250 respectively.
"The market has really turned back to fundamental buying in undervalued stocks. The rest of the market is coming off...There's a lot of profit-taking which is causing the weakening," one broker said.

"There's good reason for the market to have rerated...the prices just went off too high. Probably the (fuel) price hikes have injected caution about inflation and interest rates coming down for the rest of the year," she added.

Two weeks ago, investors were optimistic about prospects of cuts in interest rates after annual inflation came down to 17.7 percent in August from 22 percent in July and the central Reserve Bank announced measures to curb high money supply growth to clamp down on inflation.
But on Tuesday, fears of a track upwards in inflation were stoked when the Zimbabwean government announced a new fuel price increase of seven to eight percent, its third this year.

On the market on Thursday, tobacco firm TSL and glass company PG Industries each shed 40 cents to 510 and 450 respectively, Truworths dropped 30 cents to 750 with brokers saying investors seemed to have run ahead of its year-end results published on Thursday while timber producer Border lost 25 cents to 1,250.
The only winners were tyre reprocessor NTS at 40 cents up to 450 and paper and plastics producer FP Holdings which firmed two cents to 27.
Minings softened with Wankie Colliery down 25 cents to 1,100 and Falgold off 10 cents to 140. The seven-share mining index edged 2.8 points down to 1,370.38.
